key_insight: AA-ViT aims to generate contrast-enhanced brain MRI from non-contrast inputs by using a Vision Transformer that is guided by anatomy, structure, and frequency information. The core idea is to better preserve clinically important tumour details while improving image realism and contrast.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the challenge of synthesizing contrast-enhanced brain MRI when contrast agents cannot be safely or practically administered, such as in patients with renal impairment or other contraindications.
method: Uses an anatomically aware Vision Transformer backbone to capture long-range spatial relationships in MRI slices.
Adds structural guidance to preserve tissue boundaries and tumour-relevant anatomy during synthesis.
Incorporates frequency guidance to better model fine-grained image details and improve visual fidelity in generated scans.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work shows how domain-specific inductive biases can improve medical image generation. It is especially relevant for building safer, more accessible imaging pipelines that support diagnosis when contrast-enhanced scans are unavailable.

paper_title: AA-ViT: Anatomically Aware Vision Transformer with Structural and Frequency Guidance for Contrast Enhanced Brain MRI Synthesis
paper_authors: Talha Meraj, Tom Flannery, Charlie Cummins, Matt Townend, Thomas C Booth
